Physically do it yourself... make sure it's happening' — the DSP-MULTI-SEND physical proof run on real accounts). STEP 1 — WHY HE FOUND 'SQUAT': not a stale client and not a missing build. Multi-send shipped in v230 and the live files are byte-identical to the repo, but the Dispatch send card renders ONLY for non-Driver accounts — the standing v132/v186 law (a driver never sends; owners and fleet managers see his dispatches automatically). His real account's own published directory record is accountType Driver, so on HIS account the card does not exist in any version; the tester (Owner-Operator/both) and Maria's shape (Fleet Manager/office) both receive it — verified on the real backend against the real directory records. PHYSICAL PROOF (throwaway mtest accounts on the real Firebase backend, the REAL module code, the deployed rules judging every write): pairing through Connect for real; card multi-send to 5 drivers incl. a v228-code receiver; a pin round; exactly-one-tick; duplicate ticks; empty tick; a one-driver sender; a 10-round loop — every send landed exactly once, filed under the dispatch's own date, receipts delivered then seen. TWO DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED HERE: a connection REVOKED between compose and send was ignored both ways — the dispatch still landed on a driver who had removed the dispatcher, and a stale tick still sent (and landed) after the dispatcher removed the driver, with the card claiming success. Removal is local by design (v131: the entry leaves con_list, the uid is remembered in con_hidden, the pair's request doc is never touched), so the gates sit where removal can govern: (1) CP.sendDispatch resolves 'error' unless the pair is live at send time — CP._pairLive: never to a con_hidden uid; a connected con_list entry carries the send; otherwise the pair's request doc decides (accepted and not ended lives; declined, ended or absent refuses). sendDispatchToMany and sendDestination ride it unchanged, so the fan-out's per-driver line names the failure. A pair with NO record at all keeps the shipped share posture (the v207 destination-share contract, pinned by connect-pick A2): no screen in the app offers a send to a non-connection, so an unmodelled pair is the share sheet's own context, never a revoked one. (2) CP.pullInbox never lands a doc from a sender in my con_hidden (and does not mark it landed — my removal governs my screen). (3) modules/dispatch.js: the card's verdict names are captured from the card AS RENDERED, so a peer who vanished mid-send is still named in his failure line instead of degrading to 'a driver'.
